Classified experimental_evolution because the 8 non-parent deposited samples are in vitro antibiotic-selected clones derived from a single clinical parent strain; they are not independently collected clinical isolates, and the study deliberately applies antibiotic selection pressure to isolate resistant subpopulations for genomic/transcriptomic comparison with the parent. The paper explicitly cites PRJNA770945 alongside PRJNA770995 (likely the RNA-seq data). Cohort_age is not_gradeable: deposited isolates are bacteria with no host subjects. study_setting=hospital is partial: applies clearly to K65 but the 8 lab-derived subpopulations have no clinical collection context. amr_target=other because the primary selection criterion for the deposited set is colistin resistance (not carbapenem or 3GC), despite K65 also being carbapenem-resistant. amr_method=ast_result because PAP is phenotypic (colony growth at defined drug concentrations). isolation_source cannot be proposed: K65's specific specimen type is unidentified in the paper (population statistics only), and the 8 subpopulations are lab-derived (no valid source per rubric). Country=China (whole project) based on K65's hospital of origin in Beijing. Collection date range 2014–2018 reflects the 98-strain clinical cohort window; K65's exact date unknown.

notes: PRJNA1115910 contains exactly 2 Klebsiella pneumoniae sequences: His+ and His− single-colony isolates from the 2013 frozen stock of clinical strain INF018, which was collected from a hospitalised UTI patient in Melbourne, Australia. ENA taxon count (2) matches paper exactly (100% coverage). The His− variant carries a spontaneous 19,388 bp deletion of the his operon (likely IS5_222-mediated), discovered incidentally during routine lab work — not deliberately induced, hence study_type = observational. Selection for sequencing was metabolic phenotype (histidine prototrophy/auxotrophy), not AMR, so amr_study = surveillance. The isolate also harbours an ESBL plasmid (bla CTX-M-15) recovered in both variants, but AMR was not the sequencing selection criterion. In vitro bladder-model passage sequences cited in the paper belong to different accessions (SAMN17846711, SAMN17846713, SAMN21465650) and are not part of this bioproject. Patient age is not reported. The 2013 date refers to the frozen stock; the original clinical isolation date is not explicitly stated.

notes: PRJEB22119 contains 1 Klebsiella sample (K. pneumoniae ST-20, isolate 3 in the paper). The paper describes 4 clinical isolates from 2 neonatal patients at UMCG (Groningen, Netherlands); the sole Klebsiella isolate was acquired by patient 1 (a neonate) after 3 months of hospitalization. The formal selection criterion stated in the Results is decreased carbapenem susceptibility (MIC ≥ 0.5 mg/L for meropenem and/or imipenem); isolate 3 meets this by imipenem MIC = 0.5 mg/L only (meropenem MIC = 0.032 mg/L, clearly susceptible). The primary exceptional resistance feature of isolate 3 is cephalosporin resistance (cefotaxime 16 mg/L, SHV-187 identified). No specimen type is stated for isolate 3 (unlike isolate 1, which was from a rectal swab); isolation_source left blank. No collection dates are reported in the paper.
